title: Three kinds of people
hook: on that Day, the companions of the right, of the left, and the foremost (56:7–10)

segments.voice: Yesterday closed Surah Ar-Rahman: wajh, the face that remains, and your line, his face remains.

Surah fifty-six doesn't ease you in. Its first word is a when: when the event befalls. Al-Waqi'ah, the thing that happens, the event that cannot be avoided. Then the pictures: no one can deny its coming, it lowers some and raises others, the earth is shaken, the mountains crumble to scattered dust. Everything people stand on gives way. And in all that noise, the surah does something very calm. It sorts humanity into three groups.

Verse seven. Pickthall: "And ye will be three kinds." First, ashab al-maymanah, those on the right hand. Second, ashab al-mash'amah, those on the left hand. Third, as-sabiqun, the foremost. Notice the form of the first two. The verse names the group, then asks about it: those on the right hand, what of those on the right hand? Commentators hear it as: you can't begin to imagine. Left and right aren't random. The Qur'an elsewhere describes people receiving the record of their deeds on the Day: one given it in the right hand, glad and calling out, read my book; another given it in the left, wishing it had never been handed over. Commentators connect the companions of the right to those whose record comes in the right hand. And maymanah shares its root with yumn, blessing and good fortune, while mash'amah is tied to shu'm, ill omen. Then the surah describes each group. The right hand gets thornless lote trees, spreading shade, water flowing. The left gets scorching wind and shadowless smoke. And the foremost get a place near to God, which is tomorrow's verse. Notice the size of the frame. In one verse, everyone is sorted into just three kinds. Not by tribe, wealth or language, but by what they did and how they turned. The surah doesn't say which you are. It lays out the three and leaves you to look.
screen: `YE WILL BE THREE KINDS.` · `THE RIGHT HAND, THE LEFT HAND.` · `YUMN: BLESSING. SHU'M: ILL OMEN.` · `NOT BY TRIBE OR WEALTH.`

segments.voice: Picture the next few hours and find one small good thing someone will eventually do: refilling the water jug, answering the message that's been waiting, offering the seat. Decide you'll be the one who gets there first, without announcing it, then let your breath rest.
Maymanah: the right hand, sharing its root with yumn, blessing and good fortune, the word for the group welcomed with shade and flowing water. Today's word.
Your line: three groups. The right, the left, and the foremost. Day six hundred eight, done.

howItsDone: Some Muslims recite Surah Al-Waqi'ah regularly, often in the evening; its picture of the three groups is often taught alongside the verses about receiving one's record in the right or left hand.

original.note: Arabic: and you will be three kinds. azwaj literally means pairs or kinds.

trapdoor: what you thought: a picture of heaven and hell.
what it means: every person, in three kinds: the right, the left, and the foremost, sorted by deeds.
what a scholar hears: maymanah from y-m-n (right hand, blessing) and mash'amah from sh-'-m (left, ill omen); commentators read them with the books given in the right and left hand (69:19, 69:25).

chat.says: How does Surah Al-Waqi'ah divide people on the Day?
options: Into three kinds: those on the right, those on the left, and the foremost.
By tribe and wealth: the powerful, the poor, and everyone between.
Into two kinds only: those who prayed and those who didn't.
chat.meaning: 56:7: and ye will be three kinds. The right hand, the left hand and the foremost, sorted by what they did, not by tribe or wealth.
